stem:
When dilute sulfuric acid is electrolysed, water is split into hydrogen and oxygen.

$$2\text{H}_2\text{O(l)} \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{(g)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)}$$

A current of $\mathbf{x}$ A is passed through the solution for 14.0 minutes. $462\text{ cm}^3$ of hydrogen are produced at the cathode, measured under room conditions.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Calculate the number of hydrogen molecules produced during the electrolysis.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Calculate the total number of electrons transferred to produce this number of hydrogen molecules.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Calculate the quantity of charge, in coulombs, of the total number of electrons calculated in (b).

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Calculate the current, $\mathbf{x}$, passed during this experiment.

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.stem:
The standard entropies, $S^\ominus$, of three species are given in the table.

| species | $S^\ominus / \text{J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\text{H}_2\text{O(l)}$ | +70 |
| $\text{H}_2\text{(g)}$ | +131 |
| $\text{O}_2\text{(g)}$ | +205 |

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text:
$\Delta H^\ominus$ for the reaction $2\text{H}_2\text{O(l)} \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{(g)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)}$ is $+572\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

Calculate $\Delta G^\ominus$ for this reaction at $298\text{ K}$.

parts.label: (e)(iii)
parts.text: Predict the effect of increasing temperature on the spontaneity of this reaction. Explain your answer.
